title: First Contact Success Metrics and Support Surge Plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a focused playbook for the first 14 days after an activated pilot/cohort (esp. private or dedicated deployments) to maximize first-contact-success (FCS), reduce early churn, and make the support response predictable during the critical onboarding window. Intended audience: product ops, solutions engineering, customer success, oncall SREs, and support L2.

Summary (one-liner):
Track a small set of FCS-centric KPIs and run a tiered support-surge recipe (automation + human) to keep early adopters on a healthy growth path.

Why this exists (context):
- We frequently see high variance in early engagement for model-serving pilots.
- Early failures (misconfigured VPC, key rotation, model mismatch) drive most early churn and noisy support tickets.
- Product ops needs a light-weight, repeatable cadence that coordinates CS, SE, and infra for the first 2 weeks.

Key metrics (primary, measurable in first 14 days):
- First Contact Success Rate (FCS): percent of pilots where customer gets a successful inference response within 24h of initial traffic (target: >= 85%).
- Time to First Successful Inference (TTFSI): median minutes from activation to first valid response (target: <= 120m).
- Mean Time to Resolve Onboarding Ticket (MTTR-onboard): median hours for tickets flagged onboarding (target: <= 6h business).
- Self-serve Resolution Rate (SSR): percent of onboarding issues resolved via docs/automation (target: >= 60%).
- Early Usage Retention (EUR-7): percent of pilot projects still sending requests on day 7 (target: >= 70%).

Signal definitions / tagging guidance:
- Add tag "onboard" to any ticket created within 14 days of activation.
- Use label "FCS-failure" when failure is reproducible in our logs within customer's region.
- Dashboard event: emit metric fcs.check with values ok/failed and reason code (auth, network, model, config, infra).

Dashboards and alerts (lightweight):
- Dashboard: "FCS Pulse — 14d Cohorts" (owner: product-ops)
  - Panels: FCS rate by cohort, TTFSI distribution, MTTR-onboard, SSR, EUR-7 by cohort
- Pager rules (for surge): threshold -> if cohort FCS < 60% and MTTR-onboard > 12h for two consecutive 6h windows => trigger support-surge channel (#fcs-surge) + SE oncall notify.
- Ops log: append daily summary to shared doc and tag owner for follow-up.

Support surge recipe (tiered):
1) Automated checks (run continuously after activation) — owned by infra/automation
   - VPC reachability probe (x1 minute), API key sanity check, model compatibility quick-run, sample inference smoke-test
   - If any smoke fails: ticket auto-created with label onboard + FCS-failure and suggested remediation checklist attached
2) Triage (L1 support within 1h business hours)
   - Verify smoke-run logs (link), mark root cause candidate (auth, network, model, config)
   - If candidate is "auth" or "config" and SSR possible -> send templated instructions and close if customer confirms success
3) Escalation to SE (within 3h)
   - For "network" or repeated failures, SE spins up ephemeral debug session (guided runbook) and invites customer to a 30–45m pairing call
4) Platform/infra oncall (within 6h)
   - If failure is infra-related (region, quota, GPU assignment), platform oncall diagnoses and triggers fallback (route to alternate region or model variant) via rollout policy

Rosters & handoffs (first 14d):
- Weekday coverage (first 14 days after activation):
  - L1: support team primary (9a–6p local) — assigned in ticket triage
  - L2/SE: daily 9a–5p overlap slot for pairing calls (block 2 slots/day)
  - Platform oncall: 24/7 for infra escalation (standard rotations)
- Onboarding champion: assigned by CS at activation, added to ticket and daily digest

Pre-built templates and automations (put in place before pilot start):
- Email template: "Welcome + quick smoke" with step-by-step code snippet for inference and a one-click smoke runner link
- Auto-ticket generation template: includes customer ID, activation timestamp, smoke logs link, suggested owner (SE if network/config, support if auth)
- Playbooks: short-runbook for each failure reason (auth, network, model mismatch, payload validation) stored under Confluence ID: CONFLUENCE-1234

Operational checklist at activation (to run in first 2 hours):
- Verify inbound traffic and sample inference success (TTFSI check)
- Ensure onboarding-champion is assigned and has access to dashboard
- Run VPC tether test and confirm NAT/GW rules
- Confirm model variant matches customer expectations (quantization/latency tradeoffs)
- Confirm billing/quotas set and alerts configured

Decision heuristics (when to pause or rollback):
- Pause traffic to a cohort if FCS < 40% after 24h AND MTTR-onboard > 24h -> trigger canary hold + exec alert
- Rollback to a known-good model variant when > 30% of requests return consistent semantic failure (parser errors or model runtime crashes)

Post-mortem and learning loop (after day 14 or cohort close):
- Short retro template: what failed, root cause, mitigations, doc updates, and automation to add (owner + ETA)
- Close the loop: update SSR articles and embed one-click smoke link in onboarding flow if SRR < target

Notes to self / open questions (short):
- Need to align names for the dashboard metrics (should we standardize on fcs.* naming?) — @Evan
- Can we add a low-friction ephemeral debug runner that SEs can gift customers? cost estimate token run ~ $0.05 per attempt — @Samira to scope
- Investigate feasibility of region fallback automated rollout (risk: data locality + privacy) — @Luis to raise with infra

Immediate action items (next 7 days):
- (Priya) Draft email and one-click smoke runner link (due: 2024-11-15) -> JIRA: JIRA-PRODOPS-678
- (Evan) Create initial Grafana panels and set data schema for fcs.check events (due: 2024-11-12)
- (Samira) Build auth/config SSR templates and wire to auto-ticket (due: 2024-11-18)
- (Hannah) Run tabletop for surge playbook with CS + SE next Wed (calendar invite pending)

Appendix: quick triage cheatsheet (copyable into ticket body)
- Step 1: Check smoke-run logs -> link
- Step 2: Identify error class: 401/403 -> auth; connection timeout -> network; model error -> model/runtime
- Step 3: If auth/config, paste templated fix to customer and mark SSR candidate
- Step 4: If network/runtime, escalate to SE + platform oncall, book pairing session

Linked references:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (onboarding playbooks)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rtm/pull/329 (one-click smoke runner prototype)
- JIRA: JIRA-PRODOPS-678 (epic for FCS metrics and automations)

A few reminders: keep playbook light — the goal is repeatability and low cognitive load during surge. We can add more metrics later, but prioritize TTFSI, FCS rate, and MTTR-onboard for the first pass.
